questions.q: How does OneLake differ from Databricks & Delta Lake's MANAGED LOCATION setup?
options: OneLake requires the exact same MANAGED LOCATION configuration step
OneLake is optional and most Fabric items don't use it
OneLake is automatic — every Fabric tenant gets exactly one, with no storage account or location to choose
OneLake only exists after manually provisioning a storage account
questions.explain: You never provision it, never pick a storage account — it's simply there the moment the tenant exists.

questions.q: Does every Fabric item have a real, structured path under OneLake, even if you never look at it?
options: Paths only exist for items created through the CLI, not the UI
Only Lakehouses have a real path; Warehouses do not
No, only items you explicitly configure with a path have one
Yes — every Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Eventhouse gets a real path under the same OneLake root
questions.explain: This mirrors Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 45's /Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/ shape, just with Fabric's own naming.

questions.q: What makes a shortcut possible in Fabric?
options: Shortcuts are unrelated to OneLake and use a separate mechanism
Shortcuts require copying the data to a new location first
Everything already lives in one shared OneLake, so there's no cross-storage-account copy to avoid — there's only ever been one storage location
Shortcuts only work between items in different Fabric tenants
questions.explain: Lesson 7 covers the mechanics in full, but the concept depends on this shared-storage foundation.

questions.q: What is OneLake's actual pitch, described in terms of Foundations Lesson 8?
options: One copy of the data, many consumers reading it through their preferred engine — not many copies kept painfully in sync by hand
Choosing between CSV, JSON, and Parquet for every table
Requiring every team to maintain their own separate copy of the data
Storing every table in three different formats simultaneously
questions.explain: This operates one level up from Foundations' format-choice concern — it's about avoiding redundant copies across teams entirely.

questions.q: What is a shortcut, at a basic level?
options: A compressed backup copy of a table
A keyboard shortcut for creating a new lakehouse faster
A permanent copy of data moved from one workspace to another
A way for a second Fabric item to reference the first item's data directly through OneLake, with nothing actually duplicated
questions.explain: Lesson 7 covers this properly — this lesson only previews the concept.
